Capture the Empress, the Moon, even Death itself, and harness the arcane powers of the tarot to bend destiny to your will. On your turn, choose an action: earn coins, draft cards, ascend to higher levels, or capture a tarot card. Rival soothsayers may choose to follow your action, but if you have a higher level, they must pay you for the privilege. Each tarot card you capture grants you a new game-changing ability. Combine these with your leveled-up actions to create unstoppable combos. Seize the tokens of Fate before your rivals to win the game! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 1.1 Instant win condition: 2 Round Overview 2.1 Leader 2.2 Followers 2.2.1 FOLLOW 2.2.2 PASS 2.3 Tarot Cards 2.4 Common Cards 3 Game End 3.1 Soothsayers © 2025 Play to Z Objective Gain Fate tokens 🜂 through: Ascending to the highest level of each suit Capturing the highest level Tarot under each suit Trading coins for Fate tokens Activating Tarot powers that yield Fate tokens Instant win condition: 2 players → 7 Fate tokens 3 players → 6 Fate tokens 4–5 players → 5 Fate tokens Round Overview Each round, 1 player leads and the other players follow or pass. Then the lead passes to the next player. Leader Perform the top action of 1 of the 4 suits in your tableau: EARN : Gain coins from the bank, OR TRADE : Purchase a Fate token from the Trading Mat. DRAFT : Draw Common cards from the market and/or deck. ASCEND : Increase the power of each action by playing Common cards on to matching suits in your tableau in sequential order (or pay 5 coins to skip 1 level). Gain or steal a Fate token if you exceed the highest level in that suit. CAPTURE : Acquire Tarot from the market or your hand and place each beneath a matching suit. The cost to capture equals the Tarot level. Pay the cost by discarding cards (applying their levels) or paying coins. Gain or steal a Fate token if you hold the highest-level Tarot under that suit. Followers After the leader’s action, each other player may follow or pass. FOLLOW Perform the bottom action of your card in the led suit. If your card’s level is less than the leader’s, pay coins equal to the level difference. If your card’s level is greater than or equal to the leader’s, follow for free. PASS Instead of following, gain coins shown on your EARN card’s bottom action. You must pass if the leader led EARN or TRADE . Tarot Cards The Tarot cards are numbered 0-21 and grant rule-breaking effects. Each indicates how it can be activated: LEAD : May be triggered when you lead that suit. PASS : May be triggered when you pass. INSTEAD : Replaces your normal suit action. DRAFT / ASCEND / CAPTURE : Triggers during each action (lead or follow). Common Cards The deck includes 80 cards in total: levels 2-6 across the 4 suits with 6 / 5 / 4 / 3 / 2 cards per level. Game End The game ends immediately when a player reaches the Fate tokens 🜂 threshold: 2 players → 7 Fate tokens 3 players → 6 Fate tokens 4–5 players → 5 Fate tokens If the Common deck is depleted to the point that the market cannot be filled between rounds, the game immediately ends. The player with the most Fate tokens 🜂 wins. Resolve ties in this order: 1. Most coins 2. Most cards in hand 3. [Rating: 2/10] The game is likely much richer once you familiarize yourself with the deck and capabilities of each card therein. Without that foreknowledge it's a lot of picking and praying. Draft upgrade seems to be the most powerful. Overpowered? Hard to say with such limited exposure. But it does appear that the player(s) who upgrade that first, the fastest, are often the winners. Engine builders without interaction are lame, so major props to this for being forcefully, [i]aggressively[/i] interactive, though the "tug-of-war" posturing can wear thin rather quickly. [Rating: 4/10] Really dislike the theme, although it wasn't relevant to the actions.  I didn't really enjoy it, but others at the table did.

[Rating: 5/10] Smooth and solitary but then also you have to arm wrestle your opponent for the seals that win you the game. I like how different the paths to victory are but I have the sense they aren't all equally good. I want a version of this that's been developed more; I'm just not sure in which direction.  [3 plays]

[Rating: 5/10] A tableau builder with two kinds of cards.  Common cards perform one of four actions - earn money or purchase a vp, draft cards from a market, draft and place arcana cards, and upgrade cards to do more with each action.  Arcana cards improve actions, score vps, and, occasionally, let you mess with another player's tableau.  Each turn you perform a single action and then other players have the chance to perform a weaker version of that action.  Vps can be bought, gifted by arcana cards, or less permanently granted for having the highest value common card of each type or the highest value arcana

[Rating: 5/10] Really weird. Maybe too weird. I could see myself coming around to this eventually. It's a bit like Innovation and Lost Cities had a baby if that even makes sense. It's straightforward but really not at the same time. Interesting at least.

[Rating: 5/10] A perfectly cromulent game engine, but at least with four it's slow, slow, slow. Rating: Indifferent (borderline Avoid).

[Rating: 5/10] [b]2026-04-30[/b] - Came out of nowhere and knocked my socks off. Starting with the base of a tarot deck is already brilliant, as it gives some known quantity to the components. The engine-building is clever and simple, and I appreciate that most points are only yours until someone beats you in that category. Soothsayers feels like a worthy addition to the Lehmann lineage.  [b]2026-05-18[/b] - Not sure this holds up to repeated plays. The first half of the game is a race for ascension and the second half is hoping the market shakes out in your favor. Will just play RftG instead. 8>6

[Rating: 5/10] Only played once but not really wanting to play it again. I cant say what I liked or didn't like even.

[Rating: 5/10] Decent enough game, cursed by a very unclear rulebook and symbology.  Someone can easily run away with a victory if folks aren’t paying attention.

[Rating: 5/10] I get the engine building, but I don't like the (artificial feeling) switch from the small cards to the large cards. Also, the tarot setting does NOTHING for the game play and frankly disappointed me.
